notes: R-M2: happy_path_total.PLAN omits references/harness-self-checks.md (6,008 B). The read map has the file as a BUILD stage row only, yet SKILL.md reads it at PLAN memory-finalize. Adding PLAN widens the live map, so it needs a signed Read-map widening row (P11/P13); the projection leaves it out, so PLAN happy-path is understated by that much.

Signing-risk bound: the reach-lost units that REACH-A or REACH-B cannot sign return to the start sets. Up to 22,314 B of drops-to-0 plus 29,442 B of workflow or variant drops (guaranteed tree, tier reach_feasibility.tiers.guaranteed) would stay in the kernel or start files; the byte tiers assume every one of them is signed.
bias.reading: positive: the projection understates the real tree (unapplied rows add bytes); negative: it overstates

reach_feasibility.note: l3_upper_bound is the conditional tree with whole non-normative units subtracted from the byte count only, so it has the conditional row. Counters come from the P0 diff run on the projected tree with the committed policy map: unmapped_removed is every baseline occurrence no longer present at its place (the removal the relocation phases still have to row-sign); unreachable is the part of it that stays in place but is read later or by fewer workflows (a read-map narrowing). reach_lost_* count baseline occurrences whose unit still exists in the projected tree but is read later than before, whether or not a policy row exists yet; reach_loss_split classifies each by what every source (workflow, variant) pair still reads (the best single copy: a covered one first, then the one that drops the fewest pairs); variant_split is the part of the workflow/variant drops whose copies together still give every pair its start reach. signing_burden counts rows (unit ids, files) next to occurrences, over disjoint buckets; the moved-without-loss occurrences share the section-move rows (41 move ops are 41-49 signable sections, 53 counting the unheaded bake-off span's five; p10-pav-verifier-telemetry has no heading at either end and needs a destination heading). REACH-B (a section-move row covers a pure 2 -> 1 drop) would also have to cover the rewrite rows inside a moved section (a reworded parent item changes its child's parent_ctx). Under REACH-A a single-token unit can never be signed (no 2-word @reach quote exists), so the kernel section holding it stays in the kernel: reach_a_kernel_penalty_bytes. This block computes and discloses; it implements neither option.

formula.REACH_A: ids(reach-lost: in place or moved) + ids(vanishing) + section_move_rows.rows_upper_bound + widening files
formula.REACH_B: ids(in place, or moved and not pure 2->1) + ids(vanishing) + section_move_rows.rows_upper_bound + widening files; a section-move row covers the moved pure 2->1 units, nothing covers an in-place narrowing
formula.definitional_D17B: D17-B as ADR-0073 defines it (a file read on the happy path of every workflow it belongs to counts as reach 2): the pure 2->1 occurrences, in place or moved, need no row, so REACH_A == REACH_B = ids(not pure 2->1) + ids(vanishing) + section_move_rows.rows_upper_bound + widening files. The un-suffixed REACH_A and REACH_B are the narrow reading: the amendment only lets the three D17 rows through and waives nothing
formula.moved_without_loss: unmapped_removed - in_place - moved reach-lost - vanishing: occurrences that moved with their section and lost nothing; they need the section-move rows only
formula.occurrences: A = reach-lost + vanishing + moved_without_loss + widening pairs; B = section-move ops + per-unit occurrences + vanishing + widening pairs (the moved-without-loss occurrences share the section-move rows, so B does not add them)
formula.rows: a row names a unit id (all its occurrences) or a file; rows_upper_bound counts distinct ids and files, never occurrences
